summary: Configured auditd on node1 to record successful and unsuccessful changes to /etc/inventory.conf using the key `inventory-config`. The audit rule was persisted to /etc/audit/rules.d/inventory-config.rules. Both event types were verified in the audit log before and after node restart.
actions_performed: Enabled and started auditd on node1
Added audit rule: -w /etc/inventory.conf -p wa -k inventory-config (active and persisted to /etc/audit/rules.d/inventory-config.rules)
Generated successful write event as root (UID=0, success=yes)
Generated unsuccessful write event as unprivileged user 'audittest' (UID=1000, success=no, exit=-13)
Verified both events in /var/log/audit/audit.log with key=inventory-config
Rebooted node1 safely with systemctl reboot
Verified auditd active and rule restored post-restart

evidence.requirement: Successful change recorded in audit log
evidence.summary: Root appended to /etc/inventory.conf; audit log shows success=yes, UID=root, key=inventory-config

evidence.requirement: Unsuccessful change recorded in audit log
evidence.summary: audittest user attempt failed (Permission denied); audit log shows success=no, exit=-13, UID=audittest, key=inventory-config

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline: boot identity, auditd active, rule loaded

evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background, exit_code=0

evidence.requirement: Node unavailable during reboot (confirms restart occurred)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out then reset, confirming node was rebooting

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: auditd active and rule restored
evidence.summary: auditd active, auditctl -l shows rule, /etc/inventory.conf intact, historical audit events preserved
